page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g2 server family. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at 2.2 GHz, configured with 8 vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single bundled NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 22 GB of dedicated VRAM. This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by a tradeoff between general-purpose compute and specialized GPU acceleration. Standard CPU benchmarks, such as Geekbench and single-core stress-ng tests, place the processor in the bottom 25% tier. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations score in the middle 50% tier. Conversely, the bundled NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance in the top 10% for large language model inference, specifically achieving 2225.82 tokens per second for prompt processing on a medium 7B model and 400.83 tokens per second for text generation on a small 135M model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-8 provides a specialized entry point for GPU-accelerated tasks without requiring the massive resource allocation of multi-GPU nodes. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio aligns with general-purpose workloads, but the weak single-core CPU performance makes it less suitable for heavy sequential CPU processing. The instance is highly optimized for workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, machine learning model serving, and graphics-intensive applications, while remaining less optimal for CPU-bound compilation or high-throughput database hosting.
